title: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud
hookLine: the shepherd boy who became one of the great reciters (Bukhari)

lines: I LOVE TO HEAR IT FROM ANOTHER.
cards: Recite to me. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says it to one of his companions, and the man is startled. Recite to you, he asks, when it was revealed to you?
The Prophet answers: I love to hear it from someone else. So the man begins. He is not a chief or a merchant.
He is a man who once, tradition says, looked after other people's sheep outside Mecca. Today: Ibn Mas'ud.

teach.h: A SHEPHERD WHO WOULDN'T GIVE AWAY MILK.
teach.b: Start with the hillside. A story in Musnad Ahmad tells that young Abdullah was tending a flock for one of the Meccan chiefs when the Prophet and Abu Bakr passed by and asked for milk.
He said the sheep were not his to give. Hold on to that honesty; it is where the story begins. He became Muslim, stayed close to the Prophet, and learned the Qur'an straight from his mouth.

teach.h: ONE OF THE NAMES TO LEARN FROM.
teach.b: Sahih al-Bukhari records the Prophet naming the people to learn the Qur'an from, and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud is in that short list.

Ibn Mas'ud himself says, also in Bukhari, that there was no surah he did not know where it was revealed, and that if he knew anyone who knew the book better and could be reached by camel, he would ride to him.
Sure of what he knew, and still hungry to learn more, in the same breath. Now back to the hook.

When the Prophet asks him to recite, Bukhari says, he begins Surat an-Nisa. He reaches the verse that asks how it will be when a witness is brought from every people, and the Prophet brought as a witness over them.
Ibn Mas'ud looks up, and the Prophet's eyes are streaming with tears.
The shepherd's voice carried the words, and the one who first received them wept to hear them from someone else.

how: Muslims learn about Abdullah ibn Mas'ud as a teacher of the Qur'an, and retell the hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari where the Prophet asked him to recite and wept at Surat an-Nisa.

o: a one-time shepherd who learned the Qur'an from the Prophet
a merchant who paid for the first copies of the Qur'an
a Meccan chief who owned the flocks outside the city

games.q: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud — tap the pairs.
p: said with tears in his eyes
not his to give, he said

s: Ibn Mas'ud asked the Prophet to recite to him
it was the other way around: the Prophet asked him, saying he loved to hear it from someone else.
Ibn Mas'ud said he would ride to anyone who knew the book better
Bukhari records him saying it, if that person could be reached by camel.
the shepherd story is in Sahih al-Bukhari
it comes from Musnad Ahmad; Bukhari has the recitation.

games.q: you are a young shepherd outside Mecca. two travelers ask you for milk from the flock you are tending for someone else. what do you say?
o: give them milk; no one will notice.
say the sheep are not yours to give.
games.why: in the story told in Musnad Ahmad, the boy said the sheep were not his. the travelers were the Prophet and Abu Bakr.

practice: Choose a short surah you know, al-Fatiha or al-Ikhlas is enough, or one line of any text you love, and say it slowly, giving each word its full length and letting the pauses be pauses.
If you don't recite, listen to a recording of one short surah, or hear a single line said well in your mind.

wordCard.voice: Ibn Mas'ud, the one-time shepherd who learned the Qur'an from the Prophet's own mouth, was named as a teacher of it, and recited until the Prophet wept. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: 'recitation', reading the Qur'an aloud; from the same root as Qur'an.

carryVoice: Your line: the shepherd reciter. A careful voice can carry words until they land. Until tomorrow.
